summary: György Kara worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Gyula Németh and Lajos Ligeti, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and Saint Petersburg State University. He held posts at ELTE, HAS, and Indiana University Bloomington.

Gyōin Hashimoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Join Saeki and at the University of Tokyo. He served as kanshu of Yakushiji (1939–1967) and kanchō of Hossō-shū (1940).
Gé Mang Khenchen Yönten Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and he taught Shechen Gyaltsab.
Gérard Colas is an Indologist. He has held research posts at the CNRS (attested 2004, 2009) and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (attested 2012).

Gérard Fussman was a scholar of Indology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at the École Normale Supérieure. He served as head at the CNRS (attested 1994) and Professor at the Collège de France from 1984.
Gérard Huet works in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under George Ernst and Maurice Nivat, and served as a professor at Inria from around 1974.

Géza Bethlenfalvy worked in Tibetology and Indology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Lajos Ligeti and held posts at the University of Delhi (1970), ELTE, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and the University of Vienna (2007–2008).

Gösta Liebert was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lund University and the University of Gothenburg under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils Holmer, and Stig Wikander. He held posts at Lund, Uppsala University, and Gothenburg (Professor, 1955–1982).

Götz von Selle worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying at Berlin, Kiel, and Göttingen. He held library and professorial posts at Göttingen, the Royal Library of Berlin, and the University of Königsberg (ca. 1928–1945).
Günter Blamberger held a post at the University of Kassel (1993–1995) and served as Chair in German Philology at the University of Cologne from around 1995 to 2020.

Günter Grönbold worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Bavarian State Library from around 1974 to 2008, where he headed the Oriental Section from around 1987 to 2008.

Günter Schweiger worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna University of Economics and Business under Gert Klingenschmitt and held posts at JKU Linz and WU Vienna (1974–2009), alongside several visiting professorships.

H. Craig Melchert is a linguist who studied at Michigan State University, the Defense Language Institute, the National Cryptologic School, and Harvard University. He held posts at UNC Chapel Hill (1978–2007) and UCLA (2007–2015).

H. G. Narahari was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras under C. Kunhan Raja. In 1944, he held posts at the Adyar Library and Research Centre and the University of Madras.
H. J. de Graaf was a historian who studied at Leiden University (ca. 1919–1935) and under Poerbatjaraka (1927–1930).
H. Kikuchi, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, was a research student at the University of Delhi studying under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale (attested 1966).
H. Sesha Aiyangar worked in Indology and linguistics and held posts at the University of Madras in its Kannaḍa and Canarese departments (attested 1938 and 1957).
H. V. Nagaraja Rao is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).
Hae-ju Sunim is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She was a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and an Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Dongguk University (attested 1999).

Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied at Peking University under Kemo Jin and Zhongxin Jiang, and served as Director at the University of Freiburg in 2010.
